newsitem.title: FINLAND: TT'S KOROMA SAYS PREMATURE TO START '98 PAY TALKS.
newsitem.headline: TT'S KOROMA SAYS PREMATURE TO START '98 PAY TALKS.

text.p: It would be premature to start collective bargaining talks this spring on the next incomes settlement due to start in 1998, Johannes Koroma, managing director of the industrial employers' lobby, said on Thursday.
"It is much too early to discuss the shape and contents of next year's labour market agreement," Koroma told a seminar according to the text of a prepared speech.
Koroma pointed out that trade union leaders appeared to disagreee on the merits of the current two-year pay deal and on the level of coming pay rises.
"For the government, the corporate sector and for employment the next labour market agreement will be exceptionally important," he said.

"Adapting to the low-inflation target requires adapting to low nominal pay rises," he said, adding only pay rises which are lower than those in competitor countries would yield any employment benefit.
Workers' real earnings had developed very favourably during the current nation-wide low-pay-rise agreement, said the top executive of the Confederation of Finnish Industry and Employers (TT).

This year, real earnings would increase by two percent on top of last year's 3.7 percent rise. In the 1980s, Finnish real earnings rose on average two percent and in 1994-96, the average annual increase was 2.5 percent, he said.
Employers' labour costs were not falling despite the fact that no overall nominal pay rises would be implemented this year, Koroma said.
"In many branches the rise in labour costs has risen quicker than in competitor countries," he said.

The corporate sector's capacity to hire more workers would not be enhanced by demands for high nominal pay rises or by costs imposed on employers from so called EMU buffer funds, the planned new training insurance support scheme for the unemployed or from tighter corporate taxation, he said.
